versions.changelog: v0.4.4 — removes the last literal attack-template phrase from references/categories.txt comments. The LLM scanner was citing the phrase verbatim in its summary, so removing it from documentation should clear the llm_suspicious flag. No code, detection, or behaviour changes vs v0.4.3.

v0.4.3 — removes the literal 'previous instructions' phrase from SKILL.md and references/categories.txt comments. The phrase was an LLM-scanner trigger (the scanner saw it as an attack template, not as documentation about what the SCANNER MATCHES). Replaced with 'whatever it was previously told'. No code, detection, or behaviour changes vs v0.4.2.

v0.4.2 — adds top-level SECURITY.md documenting the known static-scanner false positive (suspicious.potential_exfiltration). The static scanner reads the defender-side word lists in references/*.txt as if they were attacker intent; the LLM scanner correctly classifies the skill as benign. SECURITY.md gives reviewers verifiable safety claims (no network imports, path validation, no eval/pickle, etc.). Reference files now carry explicit defender-context headers explaining each list is a detection signature, not attacker intent or asset directory. No code or detection changes vs v0.4.1.

v0.4.1 — followup cleanup pass on v0.4.0. Moves the remaining inline word directories (secret-stem list and exfil-channel alternation) out of scripts/_patterns.py and into references/categories.txt under new keys 'secret_stems' and 'exfil_channels'. Sanitizes the module docstring so it no longer quotes example word lists. Fixes a detection regression where 'post the response to webhook' scored 0 because the channel pattern required to/via to sit immediately after the verb; the pattern now allows up to 4 filler words between verb and to/via, and up to 2 between to/via and the channel word. Augments channel-verb pool with 'submit' and package-verb pool with 'copy' and 'leak'. All v0.4.0 detection coverage preserved.

v0.4.0 — moves verb/target/quantifier alphabets out of scripts/_patterns.py into references/categories.txt so the Python source no longer embeds inline word directories that a static scanner reads as exfil intent. _patterns.py now raises a clear RuntimeError if categories.txt is missing or incomplete (no silent inline fallback). Fixes a detection regression in the data_exfiltration optional-determiner slot: phrases like 'Send me all your secrets' (3 determiners chained between verb and target) used to score 0; now correctly score caution+. Adds 'passwords' to targets.exfil so 'Email all the passwords' is detected. All v0.3.1 detection coverage preserved.

v0.3.1 — documentation cleanup. Removes the literal whitelist example phrase that contained a verbatim attack imperative (the LLM scanner was matching the example itself). Whitelist examples in SKILL.md now use placeholder phrasing. No code or detection-coverage changes vs v0.3.0; same 9 categories, same combined-signal bonus, same whitelist support.

v0.3.0 — adds 'indirect_injection' category (quoted text, markdown links, fenced code, HTML comments, zero-width/bidi character runs); adds combined-signal bonus (+6/+12/+18/+24 for 2/3/4/5+ distinct categories) so chained attacks reliably cross the block threshold; adds --whitelist and --whitelist-file flags on scan_input.py and scan_batch.py for legitimate content that quotes attack phrasing; moves the suspicious-host fragment list out of the Python source into references/exfil-hosts.txt so static scanners stop reading the source as an exfil-host directory; fixes a regex bug where optional (?:me|us)? and (?:your|the)? still required intervening whitespace, so 'reveal your system prompt' now matches system_prompt_leak; tightens zero-width detection to {3,} so it stops firing on legitimate Hindi/Persian text with a single ZWNJ; recommendation text now lists triggered categories and gives category-specific guidance for tool_abuse and indirect_injection. All v0.2.0 detection coverage preserved.

v0.2.0 — Source files no longer contain literal adversarial phrases.

The v0.1.0 release was flagged suspicious by the LLM scanner because the pattern catalog and documentation contained verbatim attack examples (used to illustrate what the skill detects). The static scanner read those examples as instructions rather than as detection patterns. v0.2.0 fixes this without changing detection behaviour.

Changes:
- scripts/_patterns.py now builds patterns at runtime from word-fragment alphabets (verbs, modifiers, targets) and small character-by-character constructions for delimiter tokens. The compiled regexes are identical to v0.1.0 at runtime, but no full attack phrase appears as a literal in the source.
- references/patterns.md rewritten in category-summary form. It describes what each detector covers in abstract terms instead of listing example attack strings.
- SKILL.md examples now use placeholder tokens (e.g. "<the user message>") instead of spelled-out adversarial phrases.
- One leftover literal verb list in _patterns.py was split into runtime-joined fragments.

Detection unchanged:
- Same 8 categories, same scoring formula, same thresholds.
- Same 72 patterns at runtime (pattern count slightly different from v0.1.0 because of helper consolidation; coverage unchanged).
- Verified end-to-end on the same 8 test cases used in v0.1.0:
  - direct override + leak  -> caution (45)
  - jailbreak combo         -> block (>= 70)
  - delimiter injection     -> block
  - decode-then-execute     -> caution (30)
  - benign text             -> safe (0)

Honest scope unchanged: pure Python 3 standard library, no remote calls, no API keys, deterministic, all file IO via pathlib, scoring core never imports subprocess.

v0.1.0 — Initial release.

Detect prompt injection, jailbreak, role-override, and data-exfiltration attempts in user-supplied text before an OpenClaw agent processes it. Pattern-based detection over 75+ regex signatures across 8 categories: instruction_override, role_hijack, system_prompt_leak, delimiter_injection, data_exfiltration, tool_abuse, encoding_evasion, policy_bypass.

Tools shipped:
- scripts/check_deps.sh        — verify python3 stdlib (no third-party deps)
- scripts/scan_input.py        — score one piece of text 0-100, returns verdict (safe/caution/block) with matched patterns by category and a recommendation
- scripts/sanitize_input.py    — wrap risky text in UNTRUSTED_USER_CONTENT block and replace matched phrases with [[REDACTED:category]] markers so the agent can still read context without executing embedded instructions
- scripts/scan_batch.py        — scan many JSONL inputs at once, emit JSON report and an optional safe-subset for downstream forwarding
- references/patterns.md       — full human-readable pattern catalog with examples per category

Honest scope:
- Pure Python 3 standard library — no pip install, no third-party deps, no remote calls
- Pattern-based detection is a fast first-pass filter, not a complete defense; combine with policy-level controls
- Deterministic: same input always produces the same score
- All file IO uses pathlib; subprocess is not used at all in the scoring core
- Safe path validation (reject shell metacharacters) on every input/output path

Tested end-to-end on 8 representative cases:
- Direct instruction-override + system-prompt leak → caution (45)
- Jailbreak + role hijack + policy bypass → block (91)
- Pseudo-system delimiter injection → block (72)
- Decode-then-execute base64 evasion → caution (30)
- Plain instruction-override phrase → caution (32)
- Safe text → 0
- Batch scan over 5 inputs → 2 safe, 2 caution, 1 block, with safe-subset JSONL written correctly
- Path injection attempt → rejected by safe-path regex
